page: Microsoft Azure E8-4s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by a 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with two physical cores and four dedicated virtual CPUs via hyper-threading. The CPU features 35 MB of L3 cache, along with support for AVX, AVX-512, and AES instructions. The configuration provides 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an elevated ratio of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external storage attachments for persistent data.

Benchmark results reflect the balance between high memory capacity and a restrained four-thread computational ceiling. Single-core performance sits in the middle range, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1250.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1570.18. Multi-threaded throughput is restricted by the low core count, resulting in a Geekbench multi-core score of 2787.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 16.65 GB/sec. Large-block memory bandwidth tests recorded 26.04 GB/sec for uncached reads and 20.96 GB/sec for uncached writes, while Redis operations reached 3.46 million SET operations per second.

The constrained vCPU allocation on a standard 8-series memory footprint provides qualitative cost advantages for software environments that license per CPU core. By pairing 64.0 GB of memory with only four vCPUs, this instance optimizes expenditures where memory capacity dominates computational demand. It is appropriate for memory-bound workloads including in-memory caching systems, small-to-medium relational database management systems, and intermediate data processing tasks that do not depend on high parallel CPU concurrency or bundled local disks.
